Nissan uses SlipBots at their Mississippi facility to create fast, predictable trailer turns between the parts warehouse and the manufacturing line.
Manual dock processes created delays and variability

Nissan's dock operations relied on manual loading and unloading processes that were time-intensive and difficult to scale. Trailers often spent extended periods at the dock, increasing driver dwell time and introducing variability into inbound logistics.
High product handling increasing damage risk

SlipBots compressed trailer turn times from 45 minutes to just 5 minutes, dramatically reducing dwell time and keeping inbound and outbound flows predictable. The system required no infrastructure changes and minimal training, allowing teams to begin operating immediately.
By reducing product touches and eliminating the need for people or forklifts inside trailers, Nissan simplified dock workflows while improving safety and consistency across operations.
Operational immediately. No dock modifications, no IT integration, no production disruption during implementation.
"SlipBots made our loading process much easier. We reduced offloading time from 45 minutes to 5, which saves us both time and money every day."

Manual loading couldn't keep pace with production

Valeo's Seymour, Indiana facility manufactures automotive components for major OEMs worldwide. With just-in-time production requirements and strict delivery windows, dock operations were a critical bottleneck.

Traditional forklift-based loading took 30+ minutes per trailer, tying up dock doors and creating delivery delays. With limited dock capacity and growing production volumes, Valeo needed a solution that could dramatically increase throughput without expanding their footprint.
Dock congestion affecting production flow

Valeo deployed SlipBots at the end of production lines, where associates load product directly onto the bots. Once filled, operators use SlipBots to autonomously transport the products onto trailers, which are then shipped to an offsite warehouse.

Implementation was completed in days, not months. SlipBots required no infrastructure changes, no IT integration, and minimal training. Valeo's team was able to begin operating the system immediately, compressing trailer load and unload times from over 30 minutes to just 5 minutes and unlocking a sixfold increase in dock throughput.

By reducing product touches and removing forklifts from trailers, Valeo significantly streamlined dock operations while improving safety. Forklift traffic around the dock dropped dramatically, accident risk was reduced, and handling became more consistent. The simplicity of deployment and operation allowed Valeo to see measurable returns within the first week of use.

Slip Robotics brings fast, predictable dock automation to heavy industrial operations. SlipBot supports payloads up to 12,000 lbs, SlipLift up to 20,000 lbs—without changing how freight is staged or handled upstream.
Loads up to 40 feet

Heavy machinery and industrial components push equipment to its limits. Oversized loads often exceed standard pallet dimensions, require specialized handling, and demand extreme payload capacities that traditional dock automation cannot support.

Heavy loads also mean higher stakes. Forklift incidents with industrial freight cause serious injury, and coordinating multiple forklifts extends loading times while production waits. Slip brings autonomous dock operations to heavy industrial environments, handling payloads up to 20,000 lbs and oversized loads up to 40 feet.
Built for heavy payloads

SlipBot supports payloads up to 12,000 pounds using standardized carriers and fixtures. For heavier freight, SlipLift extends autonomous loading capability up to 20,000 pounds without changing dock infrastructure.

SlipBot+XL enables autonomous movement of long, oversized, or overhanging loads that do not fit standard palletized workflows. Custom fixtures secure the freight while the robot handles movement and positioning inside enclosed trailers.
Safety improvements at the dock

Slip removes people from trailers during loading and unloading and eliminates forklifts inside trailers. Robots handle precise movement while operators remain on the dock, reducing exposure to heavy loads, tight spaces, and uneven trailer surfaces.

Trailers load and unload in five minutes, keeping production supplied and outbound freight moving without expanding dock space or adding labor. Manufacturers gain higher throughput, more predictable schedules, and improved resilience during peak demand.

Furniture damage most often occurs during manual trailer loading and unloading. Forklifts maneuvering in tight trailers, repeated repositioning, and inconsistent stacking all increase the risk of scuffs, crushed corners, and concealed damage. Slip removes these risk points by staging furniture directly onto robotic carriers and moving entire loads into and out of trailers autonomously.

Speed at the dock directly supports product quality. By minimizing time spent loading and unloading, Slip reduces temperature fluctuations and unnecessary handling. Products spend less time exposed, trailers recover temperature faster, and deliveries arrive in better condition.

Trailers were loaded and unloaded entirely by hand. Each trailer required 8-10 employees and up to 90 minutes of labor, creating bottlenecks at the dock and significant physical strain on workers. Products also had to be moved between multiple buildings, adding unnecessary handling and compounding inefficiencies.
